title: Suggestions (beta) — copy + disclaimer options (savings + risk)
content:
Context
This doc is a copy exploration scratchpad for the Redwood Console “Suggestions” view (beta). The goal is to help users trust what they’re seeing without overpromising outcomes. We need language that is consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and that works for both self-serve (PLG) and enterprise (security/reliability-minded) customers.

Scope
- User-facing copy for savings (estimated / projected $ impact), confidence, and “basis of estimate” disclosures.
- User-facing copy for risk level (low/medium/high), including rationale bullets and what it does/doesn’t mean.
- Disclaimers for beta limitations (read-only, not one-click apply), data freshness, and variance.
- Variants: self-serve vs enterprise (tone, verbosity, support touchpoints).

Non-goals (for now)
- Finalizing naming/IA (handled in UX spec) — this is copy only.
- Legal terms update / ToS changes (we’ll route to Naomi/Marcus if needed).

Principles (shared guidance)
1) Say “estimated” early and often; avoid “save” without qualifiers.
2) Explain “why” in plain language (what changes, where it applies) + show what data we used.
3) Separate “risk” from “confidence” but don’t overwhelm the UI; if confidence is not explicitly shown, risk copy must not imply guarantee.
4) Avoid implying Redwood will auto-change production settings in beta.
5) Make it actionable: what to do next (manual change, docs link, contact CS/SE).


Terminology notes (consistency)
- “Estimated savings” (preferred) vs “Projected savings” (acceptable). Avoid “Guaranteed savings”.
- “Risk level” should be framed as “risk of regression if you adopt this change” (latency/quality/SLO), not “security risk”.
- “Based on recent traffic” should specify the time window when available (e.g., last 7 days) and freshness (last updated X hours ago).
- “Applies to” should map to route/model/region.


1) Page-level banner / disclaimer
Use when:
- Beta, read-only, allowlisted.
- We want to preempt “why can’t I apply?” and “are these guaranteed?”

Option A (compact, self-serve)
Banner title: Suggestions are estimates (beta)
Banner body: These recommendations are based on recent usage and may change as traffic patterns change. Review risk details before making production changes.
CTA link text: How estimates are calculated
Secondary link text: Why don’t I see suggestions?

Option B (more explicit, enterprise)
Banner title: Suggestions are guidance, not an SLA
Banner body: Estimated savings are calculated from recent metering and workload characteristics. Actual impact can vary due to prompt mix, concurrency, and latency/quality constraints. Beta is read-only; changes must be applied by your team.
CTA link text: View methodology + data requirements
Secondary link text: Contact Support

Option C (ultra-compact, for dense tables)
Inline note above table: Beta • Estimates based on recent telemetry • Not guaranteed

Option D (when telemetry is stale)
Banner title: Estimates may be out of date
Banner body: We haven’t received fresh telemetry for some routes/models recently. Savings and risk may be inaccurate until telemetry resumes.
CTA link text: Troubleshoot telemetry


2) Suggestion card / list row copy
Fields in list row: title, applies to (route/model/region), estimated savings, risk chip.

2.1 Suggestion title patterns
- Prefer “Enable X” or “Increase X” over “Fix X”.
Examples:
- Enable prefix caching for /chat (gpt-oss-70b)
- Increase max batch size for /completions (llama-3.1-70b)
- Adjust continuous batching target for /chat (region: eu-west)

2.2 Estimated savings label options
Option A (simple)
Label: Estimated savings
Value helper: per 1M tokens • monthly estimate

Option B (more explicit)
Label: Estimated cost reduction
Value helper: based on recent traffic

Option C (enterprise tone)
Label: Estimated unit cost improvement
Value helper: $/1M tokens and monthly impact (approx.)

2.3 Savings helper text (tooltip)
Option A (self-serve tooltip)
“Estimated savings are calculated using your recent token usage and expected performance changes (e.g., fewer GPU-seconds per token). Actual savings depend on traffic and settings.”

Option B (enterprise tooltip)
“Estimates use metering baselines and workload features over a recent window. We include uncertainty to reflect traffic variance and model behavior. This is not a commitment.”

2.4 Risk chip label options
We currently show: Low / Medium / High.

Chip tooltip (short)
- Low: “Unlikely to impact latency or output quality. Easy to revert.”
- Medium: “May impact latency or output quality in some workloads. Review assumptions.”
- High: “Higher chance of latency/quality regression or SLO impact. Adopt only with validation and rollback plan.”

Alternative (adds “Reversibility”)
- Low: “Low regression risk • easy to revert”
- Medium: “Some regression risk • validate”
- High: “Higher regression risk • validate + monitor”

Notes: Avoid the phrase “safe” as a standalone label. Users interpret “safe” as guaranteed.


3) Detail drawer copy blocks
3.1 Drawer header / summary
Pattern: “What to change” + “Expected impact” + “Risk” + “Where it applies”.

Summary sentence options
Option A (self-serve)
“Based on your recent traffic, enabling prefix caching on this route is expected to reduce unit cost with low risk.”

Option B (enterprise)
“Based on recent telemetry for this route/model, prefix caching is expected to reduce unit cost. Review risk rationale and assumptions before production rollout.”

Option C (avoid combining savings + risk in one sentence)
Line 1: “Recommendation: Enable prefix caching.”
Line 2: “Estimated impact: −$X / 1M tokens (range: …).”
Line 3: “Risk: Medium.”

3.2 “Estimated savings” section
Section title options
- Estimated savings (preferred)
- Estimated impact
- Cost impact (estimate)

Body copy options
Option A (clear + short)
“This estimate is based on your recent token usage for the selected route/model/region. Actual impact may vary with prompt mix, concurrency, and latency targets.”

Option B (mentions time window)
“This estimate uses metering baselines from the last {N} days (updated {X} hours ago). Actual savings may vary as traffic patterns change.”

Option C (enterprise + audit-minded)
“Estimate is derived from metering baselines and observed workload characteristics for this route/model/region. We provide uncertainty to reflect traffic variance and measurement noise. Redwood does not guarantee realized savings.”

3.3 Confidence / uncertainty language
If we show a range (confidence interval):
Label options
- Expected range
- Uncertainty range
- Confidence interval (more technical)

Tooltip copy options
Option A
“The range reflects uncertainty from traffic variance and measurement noise. Most outcomes are expected to fall within this range, but results can fall outside it.”

Option B (enterprise)
“This interval reflects uncertainty in baseline metering and workload variability. Use it for planning; validate before broad rollout.”

If we do NOT show confidence explicitly (v0 UI)
Add a single line under the estimate:
“Estimates may be less accurate for highly variable traffic or routes with limited telemetry.”

3.4 “Basis of estimate” / “How we computed this”
Goal: reduce confusion like SUP-19344 (“why did it change week to week?”) and “insufficient telemetry” cases.

Section title options
- Basis of estimate
- Data used for this estimate
- How this estimate was computed

Recommended fields to label (in prose; UI will render as bullets/rows)
- Time window: “last 7 days” / “last 72 hours”
- Updated: “last updated 3h ago”
- Baseline: “current $/1M tokens and current p95 latency”
- Key assumptions: e.g., “prefix reuse remains similar”

Copy block (self-serve)
“We use recent token metering and observed workload patterns to estimate how this change would affect unit cost. If your traffic pattern shifts, the estimate will update.”

Copy block (enterprise)
“We compute estimates from metering baselines and workload features over a recent time window. For auditability, we log the estimate version and the inputs used (time window, route/model/region).”

3.5 “Risk rationale” section
Need to address customer feedback like SUP-19402: “High risk is too vague.”

Section title options
- Why this is {risk_level} risk
- Risk rationale
- What could go wrong

Rationale intro sentence options
Option A
“Risk reflects the likelihood of latency/quality regression or SLO impact if you adopt this change.”

Option B (enterprise)
“Risk reflects the likelihood of measurable regressions (latency p95, error rate, or output quality) under your observed workload.”

Rationale bullet templates (examples)
Low risk bullets
- “Latency headroom observed on this route during peak hours.”
- “Expected behavior is reversible (rollback restores current settings).”
- “Workload variance is low; estimate is stable across slices.”

Medium risk bullets
- “Workload variance is moderate; batching effectiveness may vary by concurrency.”
- “Possible p95 latency increase under bursty traffic.”
- “Limited eval coverage for long-context prompts in this route.”

High risk bullets
- “High workload variance; outcomes differ materially across prompt lengths.”
- “Tight latency headroom at peak; increased batching may push p95 above target.”
- “Quality regression risk for long-context / tool-calling prompts; validate before rollout.”

3.6 “Recommended next steps” section (especially for beta)
Self-serve
“Next steps: Apply this change in your config, then monitor latency (p95) and error rate. If results are worse than expected, revert the setting. Need help? See docs.”

Enterprise
“Next steps: Validate in staging or canary. Confirm p95 latency and quality remain within your SLOs. Establish rollback criteria before broader rollout. Contact your CSM/SE for rollout guidance.”


4) Empty states + error states
4.1 No suggestions available
Option A (neutral)
“No suggestions right now. As we collect more telemetry, we’ll surface optimization opportunities here.”

Option B (actionable)
“No suggestions yet. This can happen if traffic is low or telemetry is missing for selected routes/models. Check your telemetry setup or broaden filters.”

Option C (enterprise)
“No suggestions available for the current selection. Verify telemetry ingestion and ensure sufficient traffic volume for stable estimates.”

4.2 Insufficient telemetry
We should avoid making users feel at fault, but be explicit.

Option A (self-serve)
“Insufficient telemetry to generate a reliable estimate for this route/model. We need recent token metering and latency signals to compute savings and risk.”

Option B (enterprise)
“Telemetry is missing or stale for this route/model/region, so we’re suppressing suggestions to avoid misleading estimates. See required signals and freshness requirements.”

4.3 Stale estimates (shown, but flagged)
“If telemetry is older than {threshold}, estimates may be inaccurate. Last updated {X}. Refresh once telemetry resumes.”

4.4 Feature flag / allowlist gating
We need a friendly message that doesn’t leak internal program mechanics too much.

Option A (self-serve)
“Suggestions is in beta and isn’t enabled for this workspace yet.”
CTA: “Request access”

Option B (enterprise)
“Suggestions (beta) is not enabled for this tenant. Contact your Redwood team to request enablement.”


5) Disclaimers: short vs long (recommended set)
We should standardize to 2–3 “official” disclaimers so the UI isn’t a patchwork.

Short disclaimer (footer or tooltip)
“Estimates are based on recent telemetry and may change. Actual results may vary.”

Medium disclaimer (drawer)
“Estimated savings are computed from recent usage and performance baselines. Actual impact depends on traffic patterns, prompt mix, concurrency, and configured latency/quality constraints.”

Long disclaimer (enterprise; can be behind ‘Learn more’)
“These recommendations and estimates are provided for informational purposes and do not constitute a guarantee or SLA. Estimates are derived from recent telemetry and modeling assumptions, and may change as your workload or configuration changes. Before deploying to production, validate in your environment and ensure you have monitoring and rollback procedures in place.”


6) Self-serve vs enterprise: tone + UX suggestions
Self-serve (PLG)
- Prefer shorter copy with embedded links.
- Use concrete examples (“based on last 7 days of traffic”).
- Provide a single “What to do next” CTA.

Enterprise
- Prefer explicit “not an SLA” language.
- Emphasize auditability (“estimate version”, “inputs used”).
- Provide support escalation path and validation guidance.

Suggested switch criteria
- If workspace has an assigned CSM/SE (enterprise), show enterprise variant copy.
- Else default to self-serve.
(Confirm with Marissa + Console standards; we should avoid making copy conditional on plan in a way that’s confusing.)


7) Copy do/don’t list (quick review checklist)
DO
- “Estimated savings”, “expected range”, “based on recent telemetry”, “validate before rollout”.
- Use “may” / “can” for variability.
- State what risk means (latency/quality/SLO) in at least one place.

DON’T
- “Guaranteed”, “will save”, “risk-free”, “safe to apply”, “recommended for you” without context.
- Blend risk and confidence in a way that implies higher risk == lower confidence exclusively (they’re related but not identical).
- Imply Redwood will change customer settings automatically (beta is read-only).


8) Specific microcopy (proposed defaults for beta)
These are the current recommended defaults to align with UX spec + support feedback.

8.1 Table header helper (under “Estimated savings”)
“Estimate based on recent telemetry. Actual results may vary.”

8.2 Risk chip tooltip (one-liner)
“Risk reflects likelihood of latency/quality regression if adopted. Review rationale.”

8.3 Drawer “Basis of estimate” intro
“We used your recent usage and performance baselines for this route/model/region to estimate unit cost impact.”

8.4 Drawer “Next steps” (beta)
“Apply changes manually, validate on a subset of traffic, and monitor p95 latency + quality. Revert if metrics regress.”


9) Open questions (to resolve with Design + Security + Support)
- Should we show “confidence” explicitly as a UI field, or keep it implicit and rely on uncertainty ranges + basis of estimate? (See Slack #product thread 1711006621.)
- Do we need an explicit “Not legal/financial advice” style disclaimer? My current view: no, but keep “not an SLA / not a guarantee.” (Naomi to confirm.)
- How do we phrase “high risk” without scaring customers away from any action? Should we add “High risk (validate first)” label variant?
- What’s our official time window phrase if the window varies per tenant/route? (We should avoid hardcoding “7 days” in copy if backend can return 3/14/etc.)


10) Next steps / owners
- Tessa + Kenji: pick 1–2 variants per placement (banner, risk tooltip, savings tooltip) and align with design system tone. Due: Feb 21.
- Dev + Support: validate the phrases against expected customer questions (SUP-19344/SUP-19402 themes). Due: Feb 24.
- Naomi: confirm the “not an SLA / not a guarantee” wording is sufficient + any required RBAC/audit wording. Due: Feb 24.
- Aditya/Jonas/Sana: confirm language matches ADR-0274/0275 definitions (risk vs confidence vs basis). Due: Feb 24.

Appendix: canned responses (Support/CS)
Q: “Why did my savings estimate change from last week?”
A: “Estimates update as your recent traffic changes (prompt mix, concurrency, and route usage). We recompute baselines regularly using recent telemetry, so week-to-week changes are expected. Check the ‘Basis of estimate’ section for the time window and last updated time.”

Q: “Does ‘Low risk’ mean Redwood guarantees no latency/quality changes?”
A: “No. Risk indicates the likelihood of regression based on observed workload signals, but results can vary. We recommend validating changes (staging/canary) and monitoring p95 latency and quality metrics.”

Q: “Why do I see ‘Insufficient telemetry’ even though we have traffic?”
A: “Suggestions require specific telemetry signals (recent metering + latency signals) and freshness. If signals are missing/stale for the selected route/model/region, we suppress suggestions to avoid misleading estimates. The troubleshooting link lists required signals and checks.”
